stem:
During a storm, Ekta sees a bright flash of lightning and soon hears thunder. Inside the storm cloud, strong winds make water droplets and ice particles rub against each other.

Which sequence correctly describes how lightning and thunder are produced?

options.text: Rubbing separates charges; the charge buildup breaks down the insulating property of air; a sudden discharge gives lightning; rapid heating and expansion of air gives thunder.
Thunder is produced first; the sound of thunder then separates the charges and forms lightning.
Rubbing separates charges and lightning flashes even when the charge buildup is too small to break down the insulating property of air.
Ice particles alone separate the charges; water droplets play no part in the sequence.

build_logic.mx_swap: B/D remapped onto packet mx (surface_feature_capture, term_substitution); operation_confusion and mechanism_conflation not in packet's first-four mx

teacher.key_rationale: Rubbing separates charge; large buildup breaks down insulating air as lightning; rapid heating of air gives thunder. B follows the heard-before-seen order instead of the mechanism. C drops the need for large enough charge buildup. D replaces the droplet–ice pair with ice alone.
